description: Provision an Azure Containerservice MaintenanceConfiguration via Azure Service Operator. Fields mirror the containerservice.azure.com/v1api20250801 MaintenanceConfiguration spec.

azureName.description:
AzureName: The name of the resource in Azure. This is often the same as the name of the resource in Kubernetes but it
doesn't have to be.

credentialFrom.description: Name of a Kubernetes Secret holding the Azure credential to use for this resource. Rendered as the serviceoperator.azure.com/credential-from annotation. Leave empty to inherit the credential from the namespace, then from the operator's global credential. The resource's subscription and resource group come from spec.owner, not from this field.
credentialFrom.title: Azure credential Secret

maintenanceWindow.description: MaintenanceWindow: Maintenance window for the maintenance configuration.

durationHours.description: DurationHours: Length of maintenance window range from 4 to 24 hours.

notAllowedDates.description:
NotAllowedDates: Date ranges on which upgrade is not allowed. 'utcOffset' applies to this field. For example, with
'utcOffset: +02:00' and 'dateSpan' being '2022-12-23' to '2023-01-03', maintenance will be blocked from '2022-12-22
22:00' to '2023-01-03 22:00' in UTC time.

items.description: A date range. For example, between '2022-12-23' and '2023-01-05'.

end.description: End: The end date of the date span.

start.description: Start: The start date of the date span.

schedule.description: Schedule: Recurrence schedule for the maintenance window.

absoluteMonthly.description: AbsoluteMonthly: For schedules like: 'recur every month on the 15th' or 'recur every 3 months on the 20th'.

dayOfMonth.description: DayOfMonth: The date of the month.

intervalMonths.description: IntervalMonths: Specifies the number of months between each set of occurrences.

daily.description: Daily: For schedules like: 'recur every day' or 'recur every 3 days'.

intervalDays.description: IntervalDays: Specifies the number of days between each set of occurrences.

relativeMonthly.description: RelativeMonthly: For schedules like: 'recur every month on the first Monday' or 'recur every 3 months on last Friday'.

dayOfWeek.description: DayOfWeek: Specifies on which day of the week the maintenance occurs.

intervalMonths.description: IntervalMonths: Specifies the number of months between each set of occurrences.

weekIndex.description: WeekIndex: The week index. Specifies on which week of the month the dayOfWeek applies.

weekly.description: Weekly: For schedules like: 'recur every Monday' or 'recur every 3 weeks on Wednesday'.

dayOfWeek.description: DayOfWeek: Specifies on which day of the week the maintenance occurs.

intervalWeeks.description: IntervalWeeks: Specifies the number of weeks between each set of occurrences.

startDate.description:
StartDate: The date the maintenance window activates. If the current date is before this date, the maintenance window is
inactive and will not be used for upgrades. If not specified, the maintenance window will be active right away.

startTime.description:
StartTime: The start time of the maintenance window. Accepted values are from '00:00' to '23:59'. 'utcOffset' applies to
this field. For example: '02:00' with 'utcOffset: +02:00' means UTC time '00:00'.

utcOffset.description:
UtcOffset: The UTC offset in format +/-HH:mm. For example, '+05:30' for IST and '-07:00' for PST. If not specified, the
default is '+00:00'.

notAllowedTime.description: NotAllowedTime: Time slots on which upgrade is not allowed.

items.description: A time range. For example, between 2021-05-25T13:00:00Z and 2021-05-25T14:00:00Z.

end.description: End: The end of a time span

start.description: Start: The start of a time span

operatorSpec.description:
OperatorSpec: The specification for configuring operator behavior. This field is interpreted by the operator and not
passed directly to Azure

configMapExpressions.description: ConfigMapExpressions: configures where to place operator written dynamic ConfigMaps (created with CEL expressions).

items.description:
DestinationExpression is a CEL expression and a destination to store the result in. The destination may
be a secret or a configmap. The value of the expression is stored at the specified location in
the destination.

annotations.description: Annotations is an optional set of annotations to apply to the destination resource.

key.description:
Key is the key in the ConfigMap or Secret being written to. If the CEL expression in Value returns a string
this is required to identify what key to write to. If the CEL expression in Value returns a map[string]string
Key must not be set, instead the keys written will be determined dynamically based on the keys of the resulting
map[string]string.

labels.description: Labels is an optional set of labels to apply to the destination resource.

name.description:
Name is the name of the Kubernetes configmap or secret to write to.
The configmap or secret will be created in the same namespace as the resource.

value.description:
Value is a CEL expression. The CEL expression may return a string or a map[string]string. For more information
on CEL in ASO see https://azure.github.io/azure-service-operator/guide/expressions/

owner.description:
Owner: The owner of the resource. The owner controls where the resource goes when it is deployed. The owner also
controls the resources lifecycle. When the owner is deleted the resource will also be deleted. Owner is expected to be a
reference to a containerservice.azure.com/ManagedCluster resource

name.description: This is the name of the Kubernetes resource to reference.

timeInWeek.description:
TimeInWeek: Time slots during the week when planned maintenance is allowed to proceed. If two array entries specify the
same day of the week, the applied configuration is the union of times in both entries.

day.description: Day: The day of the week.

hourSlots.description:
HourSlots: A list of hours in the day used to identify a time range. Each integer hour represents a time range beginning
at 0m after the hour ending at the next hour (non-inclusive). 0 corresponds to 00:00 UTC, 23 corresponds to 23:00 UTC.
Specifying [0, 1] means the 00:00 - 02:00 UTC time range.
